title: Concurrent kernel fallback and KV prefetch invalidation causing softmax numerical drift
creator: Emma Patel
description:
Summary: We observed a class of correctness regressions that manifest as small but reproducible token-variance/softmax instability and partial KV cache corruption when incoming requests concurrently trigger kernel fallback paths (quantized -> fallback FP kernels) while an asynchronous KV prefetch/invalidation is in flight. This ticket tracks investigation, short-term mitigations, and a planned patch release.

Context: Changes from the recent kernel-selection refactor introduced heuristic fallback to float kernels for certain sequence-length/hardware combos when quantized kernels report failure or return numerical guard rails. The fallback is executed concurrently with KV cache prefetch for low-latency warmup. Under high concurrency the interplay can cause stale/partial KV page mappings and divergent softmax sums in a subset of model runs.

Why this is prioritized: Affected customers report token-level nondeterminism and elevated hallucination rates on production models when traffic spikes trigger fallback logic. Because this can change model outputs and is data-sensitive for enterprise customers, this is P0.
steps_to_reproduce:
1) Deploy runtime-1.19 candidate with the kernel-selection refactor enabled.
2) Use a multi-client load generator (recommended: rl-client v0.8.1 harness) to send 120 concurrent prefill requests and 480 concurrent decode requests to the same model shard with batch_size=8 and seq_len=1024 distribution (50% short, 50% long).
3) Enable KV prefetch=true and kernel_fallback_enabled=true.
4) Capture a sample of ~200 request traces with full runtime logging (log_level=debug) and perf counters for kernel_id, fallback_flag, kv_prefetch_start/complete timestamps, and kv_page_version.
5) Re-run with deterministic seeding and compare softmax outputs per layer between runs.
6) Observe divergence and occasional KV page_version mismatch between prefill and decode phases.

Notes: Repro is more likely on A100 40GB and Ampere variants with batched continuous decoding. Lower device memory or higher concurrency increases likelihood.
observed_behavior:
- Intermittent softmax sums diverging by ~1e-5 to 1e-3 at middle attention layers compared to baseline.
- Some requests show mismatched kv_page_version between prefill and decode (e.g., prefill:v17 -> decode:v15) and missing entries in the per-request KV index map.
- Kernel fallback traces show that fallback kernels sometimes run partially while original quantized kernel had already enqueued prefetch completion; both paths touched the same KV slot without proper ordering.
- Resulting decoded tokens differ in 0.2% of tokens for affected runs; customers report higher downstream hallucinations in those sessions.
- No GPU OOMs or crashes reported, but data correctness is impacted.
expected_behavior:
- Kernel fallback should be strictly linearized with respect to KV prefetch/invalidation for the same request so that either: (a) fallback path waits for in-flight prefetches to finish and reads consistent KV state, or (b) prefetch/invalidation is ordered after kernel selection and any kernel-specific KV format conversions.
- Softmax numerical results should be consistent within float rounding bounds across retries when hardware/kernel routing differs.
investigation_notes:
- Collected 1k+ traces, perf counters and GPU timelines from three affected customers.
- Replayed requests offline using deterministic scheduling; divergence reproduced when two conditions met: (1) fallback decision executed by background kernel-selector thread while prefetch completes on the IO thread, and (2) KV page_version update is non-atomic relative to per-request indices.
- Review of kernel-selection code shows race where fallback_mark is set, fallback kernel launched, but prefetch callback can apply page_version updates without acquiring per-request spinlock because of a recent micro-optim change to reduce latency.
- Floating-point drift is amplified because fallback kernels use accumulation in FP32 while quantized kernels reconstruct in BF16, leading to slightly different numeric paths; however the correctness issue comes from inconsistent KV contents, not FP alone.
- Reproduction logs include timestamps where prefetch_complete (t=1001.237ms) is applied between fallback_launch (t=1001.230ms) and fallback_read_kv (t=1001.234ms), indicating out-of-order memory visibility between threads.
- Memory barriers missing around PageVersion update in kv_store.c; also discovered optimistic swap in kv index map that doesn't update the per-request shadow index when fallback path copies a reshaped KV buffer.
root_cause: Two interacting bugs: (1) A removed synchronization fence in kv_store prefetch path (micro-optimization from ENG-18290) caused non-atomic page_version visibility across threads, enabling fallback reads to see stale or partially-updated KV pages. (2) Kernel fallback path performs a shallow copy into a temporary KV view without updating the canonical per-request index atomically, so concurrent prefetch invalidation can leave the decode phase reading a mix of old/new KV slices. The resulting mixed KV entries produce softmax inputs that differ slightly; numerical drift compounds the difference but is not the primary cause.
short_term_mitigation:
- Roll out a canary patch to reintroduce a lightweight memory barrier (atomic update) around page_version updates in kv_store and make per-request shadow index updates atomic. Target runtime-1.19.1.
- Disable kernel_fallback_enabled by default for high-concurrency clusters and add a dynamic feature flag to opt-in per-customer until fix is validated.
- Add a server-side alert that tracks KV page_version mismatches between prefill and decode phases; fire P0 pager if mismatch rate > 0.01% over 5 minutes.
- Notify affected customers with suggested mitigation (disable fallback flag) and offer priority patching windows.
long_term_plan:
- Redesign kernel selection to perform selection and any required KV format conversions synchronously on a request-affine worker thread to avoid cross-thread window where stale views can be read.
- Introduce a transactional KV prefetch API: begin_prefetch -> commit_prefetch which updates page_version atomically with epoch counters.
- Add deterministic end-to-end unit tests in the runtime test harness that simulate concurrent fallback and prefetch races with stress modes.
- Evaluate moving certain KV housekeeping to the device-side (GPU) when available to remove host-induced races.
- Post-mortem RFC to be written and reviewed by infra and runtime teams (due 2026-03-25).
